scenario.title: Hospital appointment booking
scenario.description: A small fictional hospital system manages doctors, fixed appointment slots, fictional patients, and bookings. Each slot can have at most one active booking. Cancelled bookings remain in the booking history.
users: Fictional patients viewing available slots and their bookings
Scheduling staff managing slots and bookings
operations: List available slots for a doctor and date
Book an available slot for a patient
Cancel a booking while retaining its history
scenario.scope: Relational database exercise with a proposed MongoDB event model and distributed-systems discussion; no running replica set.
assumptions: All names, identifiers, dates, and records are synthetic.
A slot belongs to one doctor and has a fixed start and end time.
Bookings have active or cancelled status; cancelled records are retained and do not reserve a slot.
An active booking is the only kind of booking that reserves a slot.
Separate benchmark plan: generate 25000 synthetic bookings, compare the same slot_id lookup with and without a B-tree index, and report repeated-run median latency after warm-up.
No diagnoses, payments, real patient data, or student names and IDs are included.

entities.name: patient
entities.purpose: Stores minimal fictional patient identity for appointment booking.

entities.name: doctor
entities.purpose: Stores fictional doctor names for scheduling.

entities.name: slot
entities.purpose: Defines a fixed appointment time offered by one doctor.

entities.name: booking
entities.purpose: Records active or cancelled patient bookings; cancellation preserves the row as history.

businessRules.description: Booking status must be active or cancelled; cancelled_at is set when a booking is cancelled.
A slot has at most one booking whose status is active; enforce with a partial unique constraint on slot_id for active rows.
Every booking references an existing patient.
Every booking references an existing slot.
A doctor cannot have two slots with the same start time.

queries.purpose: Join booking to patient and slot, then slot to doctor; return a patient's booking status and scheduled doctor and time.
Filter slots for a selected doctor and date, excluding slots with an active booking by joining slot to booking and retaining slots with no matching active row.
Join booking to slot and doctor, filter to active bookings in a date range, then group by doctor and date to count scheduled appointments.

transactions.commit: Insert an active booking and commit only if the slot reference is valid and the one_active_booking_per_slot partial unique constraint is satisfied.
transactions.rollback: If validation fails or another transaction has already booked the slot, roll back the insert and report that the slot is unavailable; do not create a booking history row for a failed attempt.

noSql.documentPurpose: Append-only event documents record booking creation and cancellation, with synthetic IDs and minimal snapshots so the appointment history can be read without joining current records.

distributed.description: Proposed discussion only: consider a three-member replica set for availability and failover, and explain how replication lag and write concerns affect booking visibility. The one-active-booking rule must remain enforced by the authoritative database constraint; this is not a running replica set.
